done.why: The way on past the south shore was a grue lair I couldn't pass without something I never found. The chest was locked and the other exits were dead ends, so I ran out of leads.

about: A Zork-like underground empire. You fall down a stair after a dream of an old man who says to seek him when you are worthy. You explore caverns, a cliff, a lake and a land of shadow, and you duel a hooded figure.

moments.note: Someone or something above the cliff reacts to me. The rope twitches and it laughs at the locked chest.
The sword jumps into my hand and a hooded duel starts. The figure surrenders, but I had already killed it before I understood.
The lake shore text tells you to leave your light and sword behind. It is a clear puzzle hint.
The south passage is dark and only a can of something can get me past it. I had no way to know where that was, and I died to grues.
Death is a prison cell with the old man, who scatters my belongings along the way back in.

wished: Spare the hooded figure instead of killing it.
Find the grue repellent and the key to the chest.
Talk to whoever is on the cliff above.

lines.line: The water has the look of a cold that would open your hands for you, and would not give back what fell out of them
lines.why: Vivid prose that also works as a clue.

lines.line: It lowers its sword, and its head with it, and waits; the hood hangs within reach of your hand.
lines.why: It hinted at a choice I only understood after I had taken the fatal one.

fun.why: Atmospheric, with some good beats, but I got stuck.

engagement.why: I had a clear goal to find the old man, but little to point me toward it.

difficulty.why: Too hard: the grue repellent and the chest key were hidden.

interestingness.why: The unseen watcher, the duel with its mercy option, and the death and rebirth with scattered items.

prose.why: Rich, with hints worked into the descriptions.
